card.name: Landler
card.era: Rose to popularity late 18th c.; direct ancestor of the waltz
card.tagline: Alpine couple turning dance, ancestor of the waltz.
card.profile: The Landler is a European folk dance in 3/4 time. Couples turn under each other's arms with complex hand-holds, dance back to back, and rotate in closed hold to moderate triple-time music (Styrian harmonica, fiddle, zither). It originated in the rural Alps - Wikidata records its country as Switzerland, Germany and Austria - with its name from the 'Landl' district of Upper Austria. It strongly influenced the waltz and appears in works by Mozart, Beethoven and the Strauss family (English Wikipedia; Britannica).
card.insight: It is more Austrian/Alpine than specifically German - a shared Austria/Germany/Switzerland dance and the direct rustic predecessor of the Viennese waltz (Britannica; English Wikipedia).
